source_text: Sed ipsi de Scripturis agunt, et de Scripturis suadent. Aliunde scilicet loqui possent de rebus fidei, nisi ex literis fidei? Venimus igitur ad propositum: huc enim dirigebamus, et hoc praestruebamus allocutionis praefatione, ut jam hinc de eo congrediamur, de quo adversarii provocant. Scripturas obtendunt, et hac sua audacia statim quosdam movent; in ipso vero congressu firmos quidem fatigant, infirmos capiunt, medios cum scrupulo dimittunt. Hunc igitur potissimum gradum obstruimus, non admittendos eos ad ullam de Scripturis disputationem. Si hae sunt illae vires eorum, uti eas habere possint, dispici debet cui competat possessio Scripturarum, ne is admittatur ad eas, cui nullo modo competit.
pass_a_gloss: But they themselves deal with the Scriptures and persuade from the Scriptures. For evidently they could not speak about the matters of faith from anywhere else, if not from the letters of faith. We come therefore to the proposed thing: for we were directing it here, and we were preparing this with the preface of the speech, so that we may now engage from here in that, about which the adversaries provoke. They display the Scriptures, and with this their audacity they immediately move certain ones; but in the actual engagement they indeed fatigue the strong, they capture the weak, they send away the middle ones with a scruple. Therefore we block this step especially, not admitting them to any dispute about the Scriptures. If these are those strengths of theirs, so that they may be able to have them, it ought to be examined to whom the possession of the Scriptures belongs, lest he be admitted to them, to whom it does not belong in any way.

choices.english: to whom the possession of the Scriptures belongs
rejected: who has the right to the Scriptures

pass_b_english: They argue from Scripture and try to win people over with Scripture; after all, where else could they possibly speak about the faith except from the documents of the faith? We have now reached the very point we were driving at, the point this introduction was designed to bring us to: the issue on which our opponents challenge us. They flaunt the Scriptures, and that sheer nerve instantly sways some listeners. In the actual clash, however, they merely exhaust the strong, ensnare the weak, and leave the undecided with a nagging doubt. That is exactly why we bar this move: we refuse to let them into any debate over Scripture at all. If that is the only strength they possess, then we must determine who actually owns the Scriptures, so that no one who has no claim to them is admitted to them.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent English equivalent that preserves all nuances of the original, including the distinctions between the strong, weak, and middle (undecided) and the causal relationship regarding the possession of the Scriptures.
